exposure: Delayed vaginal misoprostol dosing interval (any interval longer than 4.5 hours)
Routine vaginal misoprostol dosing interval (every 4.5 hours)
cohort: 133 women undergoing labor induction at one academic institution
finding: Routine vaginal misoprostol dosing interval (every 4.5 hours) significantly shortens the time to vaginal delivery compared to a delayed dosing interval, even after adjusting for the delay time.
mod_finding: This study specifically investigates the impact of misoprostol dosing intervals on delivery outcomes, including cesarean section rates, and does not focus on mode of delivery as a primary outcome.
